scale: 1 = critical exposure; 2 = major issues remain; 3 = moderate issues; 4 = minor issues; 5 = no issues identified within the reviewed scope
scope: Firestore and Storage Rules, SaaS onboarding and procurement mutation/delivery boundaries. This is not a certification of all application modules or deployed IAM.
summary: The controlled procurement pilot now enforces verified identity, canonical per-hotel membership, subscription validity, backend-managed approvals and bounded transactional order creation. Browser access to supplier credentials and operational outboxes is denied. Duplicate events cannot automatically resend an external order. Public rooming-list enumeration, recursive parent-write overlap and tenant reassignment are closed. Remaining private-file access and business-schema issues must be addressed before broad commercial rollout.
reviewed_controls: Authentication, current membership, permission keys and active/trial subscription authority
Create/update distinctions and server-only ownership of subscriptions, memberships, approvals, carts, orders, outboxes and private credentials
Explicit supplier projections and denial of protected import destinations
Order quantities, line/group counts, canonical prices, accounts, revision checks and frozen delivery snapshots
Private dispatch/outbox claims, provider acknowledgement and restricted audited recovery
Storage tenant/action checks and nonempty 20 MiB upload limits
Public-token get versus list permission and immutable root tenant assignment
Rules release backup, compilation before publication, content verification and delayed activation

findings.problem: Private contract uploads persist getDownloadURL bearer links. A previously obtained token URL is not equivalent to a fresh authenticated Storage read, so the demonstrated membership/subscription revocation checks do not revoke that URL.
findings.impact: A copied contract URL can remain usable after hotel access is removed or a subscription is suspended.
findings.recommendation: Serve private files through a backend that checks current access and returns a short-lived URL or streams the file. Review and revoke existing persistent download tokens during the migration.
findings.status: Existing behavior outside this procurement milestone; not changed or claimed to be covered by Rules tests.

findings.location: firebase/firestore.rules: catalog products, contracts, groups and general settings; corresponding frontend services
findings.problem: Most non-procurement collections enforce tenant/action permissions but do not yet impose complete allowed-field, type, list-size, reference and business-transition validation. Per-hotel creation and processing quotas are also absent.
findings.impact: An authorized hotel user can submit malformed business records or generate excessive storage, indexing and processing work.
findings.recommendation: Move high-impact transitions to validated backend transactions, define explicit schemas and allowed fields for remaining client CRUD, and add per-hotel quotas before opening those modules to customers.
findings.status: Procurement mutation limits implemented; other modules require separate domain work.

findings.problem: The public rooming-list UI still attempts direct reservation and change-request writes. The reviewed Rules intentionally allow anonymous reads of a valid token only, so public submission does not have a secure working backend path. Capacity checks remain in frontend code.
findings.impact: Guest submission cannot be treated as a complete sellable workflow, and restoring broad anonymous writes would expose guest data and approval state.
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded token-scoped backend submission endpoint that validates expiry, subscription, room capacity and reservation schema transactionally, and stores internal approval history separately.
findings.status: Anonymous discovery and tenant/write bypasses fixed; public submission backend deferred.

validation_limits: Auth/Firestore/Storage emulator checks and fake external providers establish the reviewed code boundaries. Live Rules propagation, operator IAM and real supplier import/acceptance require the explicit production rollout and supervised pilot. Existing download URLs are not exercised by Storage SDK Rules tests.
